specStatements.text: Cells are the basic building blocks of all living organisms.
A tissue is a group of cells with a similar structure and function.
Organs are aggregations of tissues performing specific functions.
Organs are organised into organ systems, which work together to form organisms.

concepts.definition: The basic building block from which all living organisms are made.
A group of cells with a similar structure and function.
An aggregation of tissues performing specific functions.
A group of organs that organs are organised into; organ systems work together to form organisms.

misconceptions.question: Is any group of cells found together a tissue?
misconceptions.correct: A tissue is a group of cells with a similar structure and function, so cells of different structures and functions grouped together are not one tissue.
misconceptions.misconception: Any group of cells that are found together forms a tissue, whatever the structure and function of those cells.
misconceptions.whyItArises: Students remember the short phrase 'a tissue is a group of cells' and drop the rest of the definition. Diagrams of body structures show many kinds of cell side by side, so students label the whole group as one tissue and skip the organ level.
misconceptions.correction: A tissue is a group of cells with a similar structure and function. Cells are the basic building blocks of all living organisms; where several different tissues are grouped together the structure is an organ, because organs are aggregations of tissues performing specific functions.

misconceptions.question: How many tissues make up an organ?
misconceptions.correct: An organ is an aggregation of tissues, so one organ is normally made from more than one tissue working together to perform a specific function.
misconceptions.misconception: An organ is made from only one type of tissue, so an organ and a tissue are really the same level of organisation.
misconceptions.whyItArises: Both tissues and organs are described as carrying out a function, so students treat the two words as interchangeable. Naming a single tissue inside a named organ reinforces the idea that one organ equals one tissue.
misconceptions.correction: A tissue is a group of cells with a similar structure and function, whereas organs are aggregations of tissues performing specific functions, so several different tissues can make up one organ.

misconceptions.question: What is an organ system?
misconceptions.correct: An organ system is a group of organs that are organised to work together, and organ systems work together to form organisms.
misconceptions.misconception: An organ system is a single organ that carries out one function, so 'organ' and 'organ system' mean the same thing.
misconceptions.whyItArises: The name of a system sounds like the name of one structure, so students picture a system as a single object rather than as several organs. The organism level is then treated as the next step up from a single organ.
misconceptions.correction: Organs are organised into organ systems, which work together to form organisms, so an organ system is a group of organs rather than one organ.

mcqs.stem: A structure in an organism is made up of several different tissues that work together to carry out a specific function. Which level of organisation is this structure?

options.text: a tissue, a group of similar cells
options.rationale: A student who believes that any group of cells found together forms a tissue labels the whole structure as one tissue. It is wrong because a tissue is a group of cells with a similar structure and function, and this structure contains several different tissues.

options.text: an organ system, a group of organs
options.rationale: A student who believes an organ contains only one tissue counts each tissue as a separate organ, so several tissues look like a group of organs. It is wrong because organs are aggregations of tissues, so several tissues can make up one organ.

options.text: an organ, an aggregation of tissues
options.rationale: Correct: organs are aggregations of tissues performing specific functions, which is exactly what the structure described is.

options.text: an organism, a group of organ systems
options.rationale: A student who believes an organ system is just a single organ has no level left for a multi-tissue structure and jumps to the whole organism. It is wrong because organs are aggregations of tissues, and organs are then organised into organ systems, which work together to form organisms.

mcqs.stem: Which statement about organ systems in a living organism is correct?

options.text: Organ systems are made of one organ with one function.
options.rationale: A student who pictures a system as a single named structure reads 'organ system' as one organ doing one job. It is wrong because organs are organised into organ systems, so a system is a group of organs.

options.text: Organ systems are made of cells grouped together.
options.rationale: A student who believes grouping cells together is enough to build a body structure skips the tissue and organ levels. It is wrong because cells are the basic building blocks: cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs are organised into organ systems.

options.text: Organ systems are made of one tissue with a function.
options.rationale: A student who believes an organ is only one tissue treats tissue, organ and system as the same level, so a system looks like one tissue carrying out a function. It is wrong because organs are aggregations of tissues, and those organs are organised into organ systems.

options.text: Organ systems are made of organs that work together.
options.rationale: Correct: organs are organised into organ systems, which work together to form organisms.
